{l.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 March 1987, after the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectronal Committee had heen approved by the Agricultural and Food Products DIvISIOn Council and the Chemical Division Council. {l.2 Quinal phos granules are widely used in the control of agricultural pests. 0.3 Ouinalphos granules are generally manufactured to contain 5 percent (m/m) of quinalphos. 0.4 This standard was first published In 1980. Subsequently an amendment was Issued In this revision references have been updated and method of test modified. 0.5 In the preparation of this standard due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecnctdes Act, 1968 and the rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions Imposed under these, wherever apphcable. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysts, shall be rounded off III accordance WIth IS : 2-1960*. The number of sigmficant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements, and the methods of samphng and test for qumalphos granules.

IS : 9366 � 1987 2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Constitnents - The material shall consist of quinalphos, technical, as the only active ingredient impregnated on a carrier together with binderfs), stabilizer(s) and/or other formulants 2.1.1 Quinalphos technical, employed in the formulation of this material, shall conform to IS : 8072�1984'. 2.1.2 Blank granules employed in the formulation of this method shall be conforming to IS: 9666-1980t.

2.2 Physical - The material shall comply with the physical requirements specified in 2.2.1 to 2.2.5. 2.2.1 Description - The product shall consist of dry, free flowing granules. free from visible extraneous matter and dust except for the amount specified ( see 2.2.3). It may contain added colouring matter. 2.2.2 Sieving Requirement - Not less than 97 percent by mass of the products shall pass through a test sieve having a mesh sieve of the upper declared hrnit and not more than 5 percent by mass of the product shall pass through a test sieve having a mesh sieve of lower declared limit when determined by the method described in 12.1 of IS : 6~40-1982:j: [ see 3.2(a1 ]. 2.2.2.1 The ratio of lower to upper lrrrut of sieve sizes given under 2.2.2 shall not exceed I : 3

2.2.3 DU<I - When determined by the method described in 12.1 of IS: 6940-1982t. not more than I 0 percent by mass of the product shall
pass through 7'-mlcron IS Sieves The material retained on the test sieve shall comply with the requirements of 2.3.1.

2.2.4 Storage Stability 2.2.4.1 Heat stability - After storage at 54 � 2�C for 24 hours the product shall continue to comply WIth the requirements of 2.2.1 to 2.2.3, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2. 2.2.5 Moisture Content - When determined by the method prescnbed in 4 of IS: 6940-1982:j:, the moisture content of the material shall not exceed 4 0 percent by mass.

PACKING AND MARKING 3.1 Packing - The material shall be packed according to the requirements grven in IS: 8190 ( Part 1 )-1980t. 3.2 Marking - The containers shall bear legibly and indelibly the following information and any other mformation as IS necessary under the Insecticides Act and rules: a) Name of the material and sieve sizes ( see 2.2.2 ); b) Name of the manufacturer; c) Date of manufacture and date of expiry; d) Batch number; e) Net mass of the contents; f) Nominal quinalphos content. percent ( mlm ); and g) A cautionary notice as worded in the Insecticides Act, and rules.

Non - The USC' of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of Inspection, testing and quality, control whrch is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also contrnuously checked by BIS for conformrty 10 that standard as a further safe-guard. Details of condnions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers, may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

4. SAMPLING
4.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed in IS: 10627-1983�.
5. TESTS 5.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred to in 2.2.1 to 2.2.5. 2.3.1 and 2.3.2.

5.2 For determination of quinalphos content by OLe method, start WIth about 10 g of the sample and extract in Soxhlet apparatus using acetone/ toluene for 6-7 hours. takmg care to ensure that extraction is complete. Recover solvent as much as possible. Transfer to 50-011 volumetric flask. Add 10 011 of Internal standard and make up to volume with acetone/toluene and proceed. 5.3 Quality of Reagents - Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and drst.lled water (see IS : 1070-1977t ) shalf be employed in tests.
NOTE - 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities whrch affect the results of analysts.
